prereg._what: PRE-REGISTRATION. Every parameter of the two-route effective-diffusivity model, frozen BEFORE the model was scored against Pruijn 2008. Written by hand from the sources listed; the scoring run reads these same values out of tmesim/molecular/two_route.py and asserts they match this file. Any later change to a value here is a visible diff.
prereg._rule: DO NOT FIT TO PRUIJN. No number below was chosen by looking at a Pruijn residual. The one value with no primary source (hbd_logp_decrement) is declared a convention, set to a round 1.0, and swept with full disclosure of the value that would maximise the score.

cell_volume_fraction.source: REUSED, not re-derived: results/cellular_exclusion.md 3.2 -- Delesse's principle applied to the repo's own Xenium breast section (data_cache/xenium_breast_janesick/rep1, Janesick 2023 PMID 38114474), 167780 segmented cells, sum(cell_area)=3.2495e7 um^2, bounding-box tissue area 4.118e7 um^2.
cell_volume_fraction.caveats: Xenium expansion segmentation tiles the section, so this is an UPPER estimate; literature tumour band implies 0.40-0.72.

cell_radius_um.source: Equivalent-circle radius of the MEAN segmented cell area on the same section: sqrt(193.675/pi) um. Derived from the repo's own data, not assumed.
cell_radius_um.caveats: A 2-D segmented area, not a 3-D radius. Over-stated area -> over-stated radius -> LARGER membrane resistance group x = sigma2/(a*P) -> LESS transcellular transport. The bias is therefore conservative for this model.

cytoplasm_D_over_water.source: Kao HP, Abney JR, Verkman AS. 'Determinants of the translational mobility of a small solute in cell cytoplasm.' J Cell Biol 1993;120(1):175-184. PMID 8416987, doi:10.1083/jcb.120.1.175. Abstract, verbatim: 'the relative diffusion coefficients for BCECF translation and rotation in cytoplasm were 0.27 +/- 0.01 (SEM, n = 24, 23 degrees C)'.
cytoplasm_D_over_water.applied_as: D_cytoplasm = 0.27 * D_water(r, T), with water viscosity 6.9e-4 Pa.s at 310 K (the value permeability.py already uses). NOT 0.27 * the engine's free_D, because the engine's free_D uses an interstitial-fluid viscosity of 1.2e-3 Pa.s, which is a claim about the interstitium and not about cytoplasm. Kao's ratio is against water, so water is the correct reference.

cell_partition_K.source: NOT measured. Set to 1 (cytoplasm and interstitium equally good solvents for the solute) because no compound-specific intracellular partition is available for this compound set. Stated as an assumption, not a source.

membrane_viscosity_pa_s.source: ADOPTED UNCHANGED from the repo's already-published tmesim/molecular/permeability.py::_ETA_MEMBRANE_PA_S, which documents it as the TOP of the commonly reported 0.1-1 Pa.s bilayer-core microviscosity range and records why the bottom of that range was rejected. This choice predates and is independent of the Pruijn dataset.

logk_membrane_max.source: ADOPTED UNCHANGED from permeability.py::_LOGP_KP_MAX, documented there as PHYSICAL: bilayer/water partitioning plateaus above logP ~3 while octanol/water keeps climbing.

logk_membrane_min.source: permeability.py's symmetric lower clamp at -3 is DELIBERATELY NOT ADOPTED. It is documented there as a numerical guard, not physics, and a floor at K=1e-3 would give urea a bilayer permeability of 0.126 um/s -- i.e. it would force the transcellular route open for exactly the hydrophilic compounds whose exclusion from it is the mechanism under test.

hbd_logp_decrement.status: DECLARED CONVENTION -- NO PRIMARY SOURCE FOR THE MAGNITUDE.
hbd_logp_decrement.structure_source: Two verified primary results motivate the STRUCTURE (an H-bond-donor decrement applied to octanol logP before it is used as a bilayer partition): (1) Walter A, Gutknecht J. 'Permeability of small nonelectrolytes through lipid bilayer membranes.' J Membr Biol 1986;90(3):207-217, PMID 3735402, doi:10.1007/BF01870127 -- 22 solutes across egg-PC/decane bilayers, permeability correlates with HEXADECANE/water partition at r=0.95 but with OCTANOL/water only at r=0.75, so octanol is the wrong partition solvent and must be corrected toward an alkane. (2) Conradi RA, Hilgers AR, Ho NF, Burton PS. Pharm Res 1991;8(12):1453-1460 (PMID 1808606, doi:10.1023/a:1015825912542) and 1992;9(3):435-439 (PMID 1614980, doi:10.1023/a:1015867608405) -- over peptides spanning logP -2.2 to +2.8 'no correlation was found between the observed flux and the apparent lipophilicity' while 'a strong correlation was found ... and the total number of hydrogen bonds the peptide could potentially make with water'; sequential N-methylation raised permeability with 'only slight difference in the octanol-water partition coefficient'.
hbd_logp_decrement.magnitude_honesty: Neither source gives a per-donor decrement in log units that this work could verify against a primary text. 1.0 log unit per donor is a ROUND NUMBER chosen before scoring, not a fitted or literature value, and it is labelled as such everywhere it appears. The scoring run sweeps it over {0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0} and DISCLOSES the value that maximises agreement with Pruijn, so the reader can check that the adopted value is not it.

law.name: Maxwell-Garnett effective medium with an interfacial (membrane) resistance
law.primary: Hasselman DPH, Johnson LF. 'Effective Thermal Conductivity of Composites with Interfacial Thermal Barrier Resistance.' J Composite Materials 1987;21(6):508-515, doi:10.1177/002199838702100602.
law.reduces_to: tmesim.molecular.ecm_mesh.cell_exclusion(phi)['hindrance'] = (1-phi)/(1+phi/2) exactly, as membrane permeability P -> 0. Asserted in tests/test_two_route.py to 1e-15.

prereg.prediction_registered_before_scoring: The transcellular route can raise D_eff above the impermeable-cell value by at most the factor obtained at P -> infinity, which is set by the ratio of cytoplasmic to interstitial conductivity. With the values above that ceiling is a bounded few-fold, so the model is EXPECTED to produce spread at matched MW but is NOT expected to reach the measured 29.7-fold overall spread.

promotion_prereg._what: REGISTRATION EXTENSION for the promotion of the two-route transport model to the shipping default. It does NOT replace results/sweep/tworoute_prereg.json, which was frozen before the model was ever scored against Pruijn 2008 and MUST NOT be edited. That file records what was registered in advance; this file records what changed at promotion, why, and against which already-published measurement. Both are checked against live code: `experiments/two_route_transport.py --stage prereg` asserts the original file against `two_route.HBD_LOGP_DECREMENT_PREREGISTERED` and every unchanged parameter, and asserts this file against `two_route.HBD_LOGP_DECREMENT`.
promotion_prereg._rule: DO NOT FIT TO PRUIJN. Unchanged and still binding. No number below was chosen by looking at a Pruijn residual. The one value that moved -- hbd_logp_decrement -- moved AWAY from the value that maximises the Pruijn score (1.0, R^2 = 0.725) and TO a value derived from two open-access measured coefficient sets (1.34, R^2 = 0.718). A tuner would have moved it the other way, or not at all.
promotion_prereg.decision: two_route ON as the shipping default in compile_drug.build_profile, in `recal` alpha mode (alpha re-solved on the same measured doxorubicin anchor), efflux OFF, intracellular retardation OFF, tmesim/physics/subgrid.py unchanged and still off, vessel geometry default unchanged.
parameters_unchanged_from_the_original_p: logk_membrane_min = null (permeability.py's lower clamp still deliberately not adopted)

hbd_logp_decrement.superseded_status: DECLARED CONVENTION -- NO PRIMARY SOURCE FOR THE MAGNITUDE. Preserved verbatim in results/sweep/tworoute_prereg.json and in live code as two_route.HBD_LOGP_DECREMENT_PREREGISTERED, so the original pre-registration stays checkable.
hbd_logp_decrement.status: SOURCED. Derived in one line from two independently measured, open-access Abraham LSER coefficient sets.
hbd_logp_decrement.derivation: Abraham's LSER is log P = c + e*E + s*S + a*A + b*B + v*V with A the solute's hydrogen-bond ACIDITY. The octanol -> alkane correction is the DIFFERENCE of two such equations, so its donor term is (a_oct - a_alk)*A. a(water -> wet octan-1-ol) = +0.034 and a(water -> hexadecane) = -3.587, giving a Delta log P donor coefficient of 3.621 per unit A. The model's input is an integer donor COUNT (Lipinski.NumHDonors), not A, so a typical A per donor GROUP is required; the central aliphatic-OH value A = 0.37 gives 3.621 * 0.37 = 1.340.
hbd_logp_decrement.source: Abraham MH, Acree WE Jr. ACS Omega 2019;4(7):12920-12926, doi:10.1021/acsomega.8b03242, PMC6648601 -- Table 1, read VERBATIM. Cross-checked against Table 1 of J Comput Aided Mol Des 2017 (PMC5579141) and the open-access Acree/Abraham compilation (hexadecane -3.587, cyclohexane -3.740, hexane -3.578, heptane -3.571). Measured A per donor group from the open-access tables of PMC5830486 and PMC3477586.
hbd_logp_decrement.the_one_remaining_choice: WHICH DONOR GROUP IS TYPICAL. This converts one unsourced number into a sourced formula with one documented choice; it does not make the choice disappear. The whole measured range of A (0.16 aliphatic amine to 0.62 carboxylic acid, i.e. decrements 0.579 to 2.245) is swept in results/two_route_efflux.md section 3.3, and R^2 stays 0.588-0.722 across all of it against 0.022 for the MW-only model.
hbd_logp_decrement.direction_of_bias: AGAINST this number. Hexadecane is the harshest available membrane proxy; a real bilayer's interfacial region (ester carbonyls, phosphate) supplies hydrogen-bond acceptors, so the donor penalty for a liposome/water partition should be SMALLER than 3.621*A. No Abraham coefficient set for a DMPC/liposome-water system could be verified, so this is recorded rather than corrected for. 1.34 is an UPPER estimate for a bilayer, and the superseded 1.0 sits INSIDE the plausible band rather than below it.
hbd_logp_decrement.not_used_and_why: Abraham, Chadha, Whiting & Mitchell, J Pharm Sci 1994;83(8):1085-1100, PMID 7983591 -- the canonical Delta log P citation and the one results/two_route_transport.md section 7 named as the right source -- is HARD-CLOSED. Unpaywall (oa_status closed, empty oa_locations), OpenAlex (is_oa false) and Semantic Scholar (CLOSED) independently report no open-access copy, and no secondary source quoting its regression verbatim was located. Its fitted coefficients are recorded UNVERIFIED and are not used. Seiler P, Eur J Med Chem 1974;9:473-479 (the I_H increments) predates DOI assignment and could not be retrieved in any form; every I_H value in circulation traces to secondary quotation and is likewise UNVERIFIED.
hbd_logp_decrement.it_is_not_the_optimum_and_that_is_the_po: The Pruijn R^2 optimum over the whole sweep is at 1.000 (R^2 = 0.725). The adopted 1.340 scores 0.718 -- marginally WORSE on R^2 -- and better on geometric bias (1.03x against 1.25x) and within-3x coverage (99 % against 96 %). The single most attackable fact about results/two_route_transport.md was that its adopted value sat on its own sweep optimum. That no longer holds for the adopted value.

efflux.reason: results/two_route_efflux.md. Three independent sourced reasons it is not commensurable with the transport anchor, the strongest being that HT-29 -- the cell line every Pruijn measurement was made in -- is functionally P-glycoprotein-negative (Wils 1994, PMID 7945455, verbatim: 'No functional expression of P-glycoprotein was found in the differentiated HT29-18-C1 cell line'). 0 of 71 Pruijn compounds carries any efflux assignment, pinned by tests/test_two_route.py::test_none_of_the_pruijn_compounds_carries_an_efflux_ratio, so applying the term would change the blind score by EXACTLY ZERO. And no primary numeric efflux ratio for paclitaxel -- the one drug it was needed for -- could be retrieved.

intracellular_retardation.reason: results/intracellular_retardation.md. Built, verified against a direct transient PDE solve to 0.01 %, and REFUTED against this anchor: R^2 0.718 -> 0.606, geometric bias 1.03x -> 0.098x, within-3x coverage 99 % -> 0 %, and matched-MW within-tie rank agreement collapsing from 77.4 % to 51.6 %, i.e. to a coin flip. Pruijn's own Discussion says why: their Dmcl is explicitly a FREE-drug coefficient, and compounds that did show sequestration had it removed into separately fitted reaction terms rather than left in D. The measurement is not the quantity a retardation term predicts.

subgrid_closure.state: OFF, and not bundled with this change
subgrid_closure.reason: results/area_conservation_regeneration.md found that once the vessel field is continuous the closure stops being a no-op and inflates the F_state span 325x. tmesim/physics/subgrid.py is untouched here and its default-off status is load-bearing.

vessel_geometry_area.state: left at its current default, deliberately
vessel_geometry_area.reason: Separately evidenced and must not ride along with this change. Two consequential flips in one change makes attribution impossible if anything breaks.

what_this_registration_does_NOT_claim: That the engine's diffusivity is now correct. It reproduces 24 % of the measured spread (8.3x modelled against 29.7x measured), not 100 %.

That the result generalises across cell lines. It has been scored against exactly ONE: HT-29. Pruijn's own paper reports its asymptote coefficients moving up to 100-fold across SiHa, HCT8-Ea and HCT8-Ra, and that movement remains untested.

That any absolute number this engine produces is trustworthy. The alpha gauge absorbs most of the absolute change at the anchor by construction; what the two-route model adds is the compound-to-compound DIFFERENTIAL.
That the descriptors feeding it are right. Crippen logP is ~2.4 log units too lipophilic for cisplatin and the membrane leg inherits that error linearly.

That the taxane rows are trustworthy. Choi 2011 (PMID 21225235) measures paclitaxel at 38 % penetration through an HT-29 multicellular layer at 1 uM against 100 % at 10 uM in a P-gp-negative line -- saturable intracellular binding, which this model has no capacity term for and which the retardation term was built for and could not deliver.
promotion_prereg.registered_prediction_before_the_promoti: results/two_route_efflux.md section 4.3 predicts that in `recal` -- the alpha mode the codebase actually runs -- 0 of 12 verdicts move, and that docetaxel's FAIL persists as a FAIL marginally further outside its band. This file registers that prediction as the thing the promotion run must VERIFY rather than assume. If a verdict moves in `recal`, that is the finding and it must be reported as one.
